title: प्रवेशिका परीक्षामा दलितत गैह्र दलित विद्यार्थीको  सिकाइ उपलव्धीको तुलना {Pravesika parkṣama dalitata gaihra dalita vidyarthiko sikai upalavdhiko tulana}
nepali: प्रवेशिका परीक्षामा दलित र गैर दलित विद्यार्थीको सिकाइ उपलव्धीको तुलनात्मक अध्ययन गर्ने क्रममा हिन्दुवर्णाश्रम व्यवस्थामा शुद्र वर्ग छोइछिटा लाग्ने भनि जनिएका कामी, दमाई,सार्की, तेली डोम, गाइने जातलाई दलित र सो बाहेकका अन्य जातलाई गैर दलित भनि अध्ययन गरेको छु ।  प्रवेशिका परीक्षामा दलित विद्यार्थीको उपलव्धी गैर दलित विद्यार्थीको भन्दा कस्तो रहेछ भनि आदर्श उ.मा.वि. इलाम स्रोतकेन्द्र अन्तर्गतका ५ माध्यमिक विद्यालयको पाँच वर्षको प्रवेशिका परीक्षाको नतिजाको तुलनात्मक अध्ययन गरिएको छ । अध्ययनको क्रममा प्रवेशिका परीक्षामा दलित विद्यार्थीको शैक्षिक उपलव्धी कति छ ? दलित गैर दलित विद्यार्थीको शैक्षिक उपलव्धीका तुलनात्मक अवस्था कस्तो रहेको छ, दलित विद्यार्थीको उपलव्धी स्तर बढाउन के गर्नुपर्छ जस्ता विषयमा अध्ययन गरिएको छ ।  अध्ययनको सैेद्धान्तिक खाकाको रूपमा कार्लमाक्स, म्याक्स वेवर, गेहार्ड लेन्सकी तथा मास्लोका सिद्धान्तहरूलाई प्रयोग गरिएको छ । पूर्व साहित्यहरूको समीक्षा गर्ने क्रममा समसामयिक लेख रचना तथा अध्ययन प्रतिवेदनहरूको समीक्षा गरिएको छ । अध्ययनका लागि इलाम जिल्लाको आदर्श उ. मा.वि. स्रोत केन्द्र अन्र्तगतका नमूनाको रुपमा छनौट गरिएको छ । तोकिएका उद्देश्यहरू पूरा गर्नका लागि प्राथमिक तथा द्वितीय दुवै प्रकारका श्रोतहरूबाट तथ्याङ्क सङ्कलन गरिएको छ । प्राथमिक तथ्याङ्क सङ्कलनको लागि प्रश्नावलीको माध्यमबाट चिट्ठा पद्धति अनुसार छनोट गरिएका नमूना छनोटमा परेका प्रत्येक विद्यालयका २ शिक्षक, ५ दलित विद्यार्थी, ५ दलित अभिभावक, २ जना विद्यालय निरीक्षकहरूको मत सङ्कलनको लागि तथ्याङ्क सङ्कलन फारमको प्रयोग गरी विद्यालयको एस. एल. सी. मार्कलेजरबाट २०६० देखि २०६४ सम्मको हरेक वर्षको १० ÷१० जनाको दरले दलित तथा गैर दलित विद्यार्थीहरूको एस. एल. सी. परीक्षाको उपलब्धि लिइएको छ । यसको तथ्याङ्कको प्रस्तुति तथा ब्याख्या विश्लेषणको गणितीय प्रस्तुतिको कारणले यो अनुसन्धान परिमाणात्मक अनुसन्धान बन्न पुगेको छ ।  एस.एल.सी. परीक्षामा दलित विद्यार्थीहरूको औषत उपलब्धि ४२.७८५ तथा गैर दलित विद्यार्थीहरूको उपलब्धि ४८.७४५ रहेको पाइयो । दलित विद्यार्थी प्रति विद्यालय , शिक्षक तथा अन्य विद्यार्थीहरूबाट अन्य विद्यार्थी सरह समान व्यवहार गरेको पाइयो । पाठ्यक्रम तथा पाठ्यपुस्तकले समेत दलित विद्यार्थीहरूलाई विशेष प्रोत्साहन दिन नसकेपनि विभेद नगरेको पाइयो । शिक्षक , अभिभावक तथा विद्यालय निरीक्षकहरू सबैले दलित विद्यार्थीहरूलाई शिक्षाको मूल प्रवाहमा समेट्न समताको सिद्धान्तको आधारमा व्यवहार गर्नुपर्दछ  भन्ने कुरामा जोड दिएको पाइयो ।  दलित विद्यार्थीको औषत शैक्षिक उपलब्धि कम देखिएको हुँदा यस तर्फ ध्यान दिई उनीहरूको शैक्षिक उपलब्धि बृद्धि गर्ने कार्यक्रमहरू सञ्चालन गर्नुपर्ने देखियो । दलित विद्यार्थीलाई विशेष प्रोत्साहन हुने गरी पाठ्यक्रम तथा पाठ्यपुस्तक तयार गर्नुपर्ने, दलित अभिभावकहरूमा चेतना अभिबृद्धि गर्न सचेतना कार्यक्रम सञ्चालन गर्नुपर्ने, दलित छात्रबृत्तिमा रकम थप गर्ने, अतिरिक्त कक्षाहरू सञ्चालन गर्ने, विद्यालय ब्यवस्थापन समिति, अभिभावक भेला लगायतका कार्यक्रममा दलित अभिभावकहरूलाई अनिवार्य संलग्न गराउने, विद्यालयमा दलित मैत्री वातावरणको विकास गर्ने, दलित  विद्यार्थीहरू बीच प्रतिस्पर्धा गराइ पुरस्कृत गर्ने जस्ता कार्यक्रहरू विद्यालयले गर्न सके दलित विद्यार्थीहरूको शैक्षिक उपलब्धि बृद्धि गर्न सहयोग पुग्दछ
american_english: In the course of conducting a comparative study of the learning achievement of Dalit and non-Dalit students in the SLC examination, I have defined as Dalits the Kami, Damai, Sarki, Teli, Dom, and Gaine castes, who were identified as Shudras in the Hindu varna system and considered untouchable, and I have defined all other castes as non-Dalits. A comparative study was carried out of the five-year SLC examination results of five secondary schools under the Adarsha Secondary School, Ilam Resource Center to examine how the achievement of Dalit students compared with that of non-Dalit students in the SLC examination. In the course of the study, issues such as what the educational achievement of Dalit students in the SLC examination is, what the comparative state of the educational achievement of Dalit and non-Dalit students is, and what needs to be done to raise the achievement level of Dalit students were examined. The theories of Karl Marx, Max Weber, Gerhard Lenski, and Maslow were used as the theoretical framework for the study. In the course of reviewing previous literature, contemporary writings and study reports were reviewed. For the study, schools under the Adarsha Secondary School Resource Center in Ilam district were selected as the sample. To fulfill the stated objectives, data were collected from both primary and secondary sources. For the collection of primary data, opinions were gathered through questionnaires using a lottery method from 2 teachers, 5 Dalit students, 5 Dalit parents, and 2 school inspectors from each of the schools selected in the sample, and the SLC examination achievement of Dalit and non-Dalit students was taken from the schools' SLC mark ledgers at the rate of 10 students from each group per year from 2060 to 2064 BS. Because of the mathematical presentation of the data and its explanation and analysis, this research became a quantitative study. The average achievement of Dalit students in the SLC examination was found to be 42.785, and that of non-Dalit students was found to be 48.745. It was found that schools, teachers, and other students treated Dalit students equally, just like other students. Although the curriculum and textbooks could not provide special encouragement to Dalit students, it was found that they did not discriminate against them. Teachers, parents, and school inspectors all emphasized that Dalit students should be treated on the basis of the principle of equality in order to bring them into the mainstream of education. Since the average educational achievement of Dalit students was found to be low, it was seen that attention should be paid to this and programs should be implemented to increase their educational achievement. If schools can carry out activities such as preparing curricula and textbooks that provide special encouragement to Dalit students, conducting awareness programs to increase consciousness among Dalit parents, increasing the amount of Dalit scholarships, running additional classes, ensuring the mandatory involvement of Dalit parents in programs such as school management committees and parent meetings, developing a Dalit-friendly environment in schools, and organizing competitions among Dalit students and rewarding them, this would help increase the educational achievement of Dalit students.

informal_english: While doing a comparative study of how Dalit and non-Dalit students got on in the SLC examination, I’ve classed the Kami, Damai, Sarki, Teli, Dom, and Gaine castes—who were labelled as Shudras in the Hindu varna system and treated as untouchable—as Dalits, and I’ve classed all the other castes as non-Dalits. I did a comparative study of five years’ worth of SLC exam results from five secondary schools under the Adarsha Secondary School, Ilam Resource Centre to see how Dalit students’ achievement stacked up against that of non-Dalit students in the SLC exam. As part of the study, I looked into things like what the educational achievement of Dalit students in the SLC exam actually is, how the educational achievement of Dalit and non-Dalit students compares, and what needs to be done to lift the achievement levels of Dalit students. I used the theories of Karl Marx, Max Weber, Gerhard Lenski, and Maslow as the theoretical framework for the study. When reviewing earlier literature, I went over contemporary writings and study reports. For the study, schools under the Adarsha Secondary School Resource Centre in Ilam district were picked as the sample. To meet the stated aims, I gathered data from both primary and secondary sources. For the primary data, I collected opinions through questionnaires using a lottery method from 2 teachers, 5 Dalit students, 5 Dalit parents, and 2 school inspectors from each of the sampled schools, and I took the SLC exam achievement of Dalit and non-Dalit students from the schools’ SLC mark ledgers at a rate of 10 students from each group per year from 2060 to 2064 BS. Because the data was presented and explained mathematically, this ended up being a quantitative study. It turned out that the average achievement of Dalit students in the SLC exam was 42.785, while that of non-Dalit students was 48.745. It was found that schools, teachers, and other students treated Dalit students fairly, just like everyone else. Even though the curriculum and textbooks didn’t really give Dalit students any special encouragement, they didn’t discriminate against them either. Teachers, parents, and school inspectors all reckoned Dalit students should be treated on the basis of equality so they can be brought into the mainstream of education. Since the average educational achievement of Dalit students was on the low side, it was clear that we need to pay attention to this and run programmes to boost their educational achievement. If schools can get stuck into things like putting together curricula and textbooks that give Dalit students a bit of extra encouragement, running awareness programmes to lift consciousness among Dalit parents, bumping up the amount of Dalit scholarships, running extra classes, making sure Dalit parents are mandatorily involved in things like school management committees and parent meetings, creating a Dalit-friendly vibe at school, and organising competitions among Dalit students and rewarding them, that’d go a long way towards lifting the educational achievement of Dalit students.
translator_notes: Informal flavour rendered as New Zealand casual. 'प्रवेशिका परीक्षा' and 'एस.एल.सी. परीक्षा' are retained as SLC examination in line with common usage for the same qualification; 'आदर्श उ.मा.वि. इलाम स्रोतकेन्द्र' rendered as Adarsha Secondary School, Ilam Resource Center/Centre. The final sentence in the source lacks a closing danda; this is preserved in meaning without adding content. Numbers, years (2060–2064 BS), and names kept as in source.
